differentiation.support: Provide the student notes open at the cell membrane and selectively permeable definitions so learners can follow what crosses and what is refused before judging the solid-wall claim.

differentiation.stretch: Ask learners to name which scene proved that the membrane chooses what crosses before they take the exit ticket.

activities.title: Cells team up: the organisation ladder

assessmentPoints: Labelling answers in the opening activity
Missing-structures answers in the second activity and the closing worksheet
successCriteria: I can label the cell wall, membrane, nucleus, chloroplast and large vacuole on a plant cell and say the animal cell has no wall, chloroplast or large vacuole
I can state that the nucleus controls the cell, the chloroplast traps light to make food and the mitochondrion releases energy from food
objectives.text: Label the main structures of plant and animal cells and state each job

assessmentPoints: Gatekeeper answers in the third activity
Worksheet answers checked in the closing activity
successCriteria: I can explain that the membrane lets food and oxygen cross in and waste cross out while refusing harmful particles
I can contrast the selectively permeable membrane with the plant cell wall, which is fully permeable and gives shape and strength
objectives.text: Explain the cell membrane as selectively permeable, not a solid wall

assessmentPoints: Turgor answers in the fifth activity
Ladder answers in the sixth activity and the closing exit ticket
successCriteria: I can explain that a full vacuole pushes the membrane against the wall so the cell is turgid, and that losing water makes cells flaccid so the plant wilts
I can order the ladder as cell, tissue, organ, system, as in leaf cell, leaf tissue, leaf, shoot system
objectives.text: Describe turgor in a plant cell and order the organisation ladder from cell to system
